newsitem.title: DUBAI: Germany, UAE plan investment pact - Rexrodt.
newsitem.headline: Germany, UAE plan investment pact - Rexrodt.

text.p: Germany and the United Arab Emirates will sign a bilateral investment promotion and protection pact in the next few days, German Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt said on Monday.

"We have a special contract for investment protection and promotion initialled, which gives the German government the possibility to take over the guarantee for political risks," he told Reuters at a German trade show in Dubai.
He said the agreement, initialled "some days ago", would be signed in "the next few days" once a new UAE cabinet is formed.
The government resigned eight days ago and President Sheikh Zaid bin Sultan al-Nahayan asked the prime minister to form a new cabinet.
Rexrodt said the Gulf was becoming increasingly important to Germany. "German industry was traditionally strong in Iran, but the focus has moved from Iran to Saudi Arabia and the Gulf," he said.

Latest German embassy figures show trade between Germany and the six Gulf states -- Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar, Oman and the UAE was worth some 9.25 billion marks ($5.5 billion) in 1995. Most of this represents German exports to the Gulf.
In 1995, UAE-German trade reached almost 2.6 billion marks.
